title: Jailer 2 Opens October 15 Amid Revenue-Sharing Row, Rs 38 Crore Advance Bookings and a Rs 1,000 Crore Dream
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel has taken Rs 38.09 crore in domestic advance bookings ahead of Thursday's release, but a dispute over a 75% revenue-share demand has clouded its Hindi release — while trade trackers debate whether it can become the first Tamil film to cross Rs 1,000 crore.
body:
• Jailer 2, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, releases on Thursday, October 15, with Rajinikanth returning as Muthuvel "Tiger" Pandian.
  • Domestic advance bookings have reached Rs 38.09 crore gross, including Rs 21.75 crore for opening day; Chennai leads individual markets with Rs 12.35 crore.
  • A revenue-sharing dispute — theatre owners refusing a reported 75% share demand — has clouded the Hindi release, which the team says will proceed via Pen Marudhar through regional and independent theatres in North India.
  • Trade estimates for the full run range from Rs 650-800 crore to the Rs 1,000 crore upside; the original Jailer grossed about Rs 604 crore worldwide.

Rajinikanth returns as Muthuvel "Tiger" Pandian on Thursday, and Jailer 2 arrives with the largest expectations attached to any Tamil release this year — and a distribution fight to match. The action-comedy sequel, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Kalanithi Maran's Sun Pictures, has collected Rs 38.09 crore in domestic advance bookings ahead of its October 15 release, with Rs 21.75 crore of that for opening day alone, according to trade reporting carried by Latestly.

The Tamil version accounts for the lion's share, Rs 33.95 crore, and Chennai leads individual markets with Rs 12.35 crore. The film has been certified UA 16+ by the CBFC with a runtime of 165 minutes, and Sun Pictures has secured an interim injunction from the Madras High Court against unauthorised online exhibition to combat piracy ahead of release. It is also, according to Cinema Express, the first Rajinikanth film to receive a wide IMAX release.

The revenue-sharing row

The release has been clouded by a dispute over revenue sharing: theatre owners have refused a reported 75 per cent share demand, raising the prospect that the Hindi version might not screen in major multiplex chains. The film's team later clarified that the Hindi release would proceed as scheduled on October 15, with Pen Marudhar Entertainment handling distribution, likely through regional and independent theatres across North India. Whether an eleventh-hour agreement restores the major chains remains the open question on the eve of release — and it matters to the film's ceiling, because the Hindi market is where the upside case lives.

The Rs 1,000 crore question, in numbers

The benchmarks are clear. Of the top three Tamil grossers worldwide, two belong to Rajinikanth: 2.0 at Rs 691 crore and Jailer at Rs 604.50 crore, with Vijay's Leo second at Rs 605.90 crore, according to Variety India. Rajinikanth's Coolie set the current Tamil opening-day benchmark with a reported Rs 151 crore worldwide in 2025.

https://x.com/jerinGeorgekut2/status/2109873588421775851

Chennai-based trade tracker Ramesh Bala told Variety India the film has the potential to reach Rs 1,000 crore if it gets good exposure in the Hindi market, pointing to cameos by Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar and Hrithik Roshan as cross-industry draws. More conservative pre-release estimates put the worldwide opening day at Rs 100-140 crore and the full run at Rs 650-800 crore with strong word of mouth — treating Rs 1,000 crore as an ambitious upside scenario rather than the baseline. Koimoi's tracker expects a Rs 120 crore-plus worldwide opening day.

Cast and what's at stake

Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa and Rithvik reprise their roles, joined by SJ Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Vidya Balan, Anna Rajan and Jatin Sarna, with cameos expected from Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff, Vijay Sethupathi and Hrithik Roshan. Anirudh Ravichander returns as composer. The reported budget is Rs 250-350 crore, which makes the opening weekend a genuine financial event for Sun Pictures, not just a fan celebration.

For diaspora audiences

US and other overseas screenings begin with the October 15 worldwide release, and the IMAX rollout gives diaspora fans in major metros the format Rajinikanth releases have not previously had at this scale. Given the Hindi-chain dispute in India, overseas performance — historically strong for Rajinikanth — will be watched as an early indicator of whether the film's run points toward Rs 800 crore or something larger. Advance booking in North America is through the usual major chains' apps and Fandango; check local listings for IMAX showtimes, which are the first to sell out for event releases of this size.
